proposed.text: Under the 2024 IRR (Trap #49), what percentage of seats in an assembly hall must be designated as wheelchair spaces, and what replaced the old tiered table?

options.text: 2% of total seating capacity under the 2024 IRR, replacing the old 4-per-300-seat tiered table, ensuring greater accessibility
3% of total seating capacity under the 2024 IRR, replacing the old tiered table (4–50 seats → 2 spaces, etc.)
5% of total seating capacity under the 2024 IRR, a single flat rate for all assembly occupancies, simplifying compliance
4% of total seating capacity under the 2024 IRR, replacing the old variable-percentage formula, providing a more uniform standard

rationale.summary: Trap #49: 2024 IRR replaces the old tiered table with a flat 3% of total seating capacity for wheelchair spaces.
rationale.explanation: Trap #49 in the article. The old BP 344 IRR used a tiered table: 4–50 seats → 2 wheelchair spaces; 51–300 → 4 spaces; 301–500 → 6 spaces; 500+ → additional 1 per 100. The 2024 IRR replaced this with a single flat rule: 3% of total seating capacity shall be wheelchair spaces (Sec. 4 App. D). Additionally, 5% of general waiting area seating must be designated priority seats for PWDs — a separate provision. The exam tests whether candidates know the new flat rate versus the old tiered table.
common_misconceptions: Using the old tiered table for a 2024 IRR question — the flat 3% rule replaced all tiered formulas
Confusing the 3% wheelchair space quota with the 5% priority seating quota — these are two distinct requirements

proposed.explanation: 2024 IRR: 3% flat rate for wheelchair spaces in assembly (plus 5% priority seating) — the old tiered table is superseded.
proposed.code_citation: BP 344 2024 IRR Sec. 4 App. D; Trap #49
